scope: Proposition 3.13 (Centers and regular systems) of the manuscript “Path selection and an elliptic inequality on degenerating Ricci-flat trees” (preprints/Path-selection-and-an-elliptic-inequality-on-degenerating-Ricci-flat-trees-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 351 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a49f3dc92b22b888), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 19-20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For a distinguished sequence of m lengths tending to infinity, there are centers L∗ 1, . . . , L∗ m, differing from the sequence values by bounded additive amounts, and a regular system on a domain base with the following additional properties. 19 (a) The system contains the centers, ebL∗ i for every real b, and every admissible family evaluated at these centers. (b) Every finite expression built with the allowed analytic operations has coefficient formulas on a common connected domain of the base and a common ordinary-parameter neighborhood. The same formulas remain valid to all orders on paths preserving its finite preparation data. Remainder sectors and thresholds may depend on order. (c) On the path families, the grouped centers have the form ciX + D∗ i , ci > 0, where the positive magnitudes of the unbounded D∗ i are slower centers. All required quadratic holomorphy domains are reached after narrowing the clock sectors. (d) For a nonempty tuple, its path families can be chosen so that the last clock is the selected fastest center X. Every center is O(X), and one of the centers equals X. In particular the last clock is comparable to maxi L∗ i , independently of which finite expression requirements are imposed.
